message.content:
Build the vanilla Minecraft 26.2 main menu and menu screens for a browser recreation. Project: C:\Users\zht\Documents\Qoder\2026-11-01\4194ac07\webcraft26 (TypeScript + Vite + WebGL2). It has official local 26.2 assets under public/mc (generated from the user's own client; do not redistribute) and a game that currently boots straight into the world.

FILE BOUNDARIES: You own new files src/menu.ts and src/menu.css (plus optional src/menuAssets.ts). You may edit scripts/build-assets.mjs ONLY to copy additional official menu/panorama assets into public/mc. Do NOT edit src/main.ts, index.html, src/style.css, src/hud.ts, src/assets.ts, src/world.ts, src/renderer.ts, src/mesher.ts, package.json, or any other file. The main agent will integrate your module. Do not edit public/mc files by hand. Do not run the dev server or browser; another agent owns verification. You may run `npm run assets` (it reads G:/ck-web26/vanilla/assets/minecraft and writes public/mc) and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

Goal: a self-contained module that renders an authentic-looking vanilla 26.2 menu shell over the game:
- Main menu with the official panorama (6 faces: textures/gui/title/background/panorama_0..5.png) slowly rotating as a cubemap, official title logo (textures/gui/title/minecraft.png or equivalent), splash text, and vanilla-style buttons. Screens: Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Options, Quit.
- Use the official vanilla bitmap font if practical: inspect src/font.ts and src/assets.ts to reuse VanillaFont (find the font texture/manifest paths and widths) without needing the whole game LoadedAssets. If that is too coupled, implement a small canvas bitmap-font renderer using the same font PNG and metadata. Do NOT settle for an arbitrary system font if the vanilla one is available. UI should be crisp/pixelated, centered, 2x GUI scale, buttons from official widget sprites if available (public/mc/gui/sprites/widget/button.png + button_highlighted.png; build-assets currently copies some GUI sprites - extend it if needed).
- Main menu buttons (top to bottom): Singleplayer, Multiplayer, Options..., Quit Game. Bottom-left shows version text; bottom-right copyright-style line. Add small language/accessibility icon buttons if assets make it easy. Must be usable with mouse/touch/keyboard (Enter/Escape), focus states, and respect pixel GUI scaling.
- Singleplayer screen: list local worlds (at minimum a default "World" entry persisted in localStorage), Create New World button (can open a small vanilla-style screen with name/seed fields and game mode toggle), Play Selected World; Back. The module should call a callback with the chosen world settings.
- Multiplayer screen: server list persisted in localStorage with Add Server and Direct Connect screens; each entry shows name/address/status; Join Selected Server; Back. Callback with address, forwarding to a future WebSocket Paper bridge.
- Options screen: Graphics sliders/cycles for Quality (Auto/Low/Medium/High/Ultra), Render Distance (4-16), FOV (30-110), Pixel Filtering (Off/Nearest/Linear), Shader Effects on/off, Touch Controls (Auto/On/Off); Audio volume; Done. Persist all settings in localStorage and expose them via getSettings()/onSettingsChange. This is critical for the user's "dynamically adjust based on configuration" request.
- Optional but valuable: pause menu API (Back to Game, Options, Save and Quit to Title) and a loading screen helper showing progress text/bar.
- API design: export class VanillaMenu with constructor(root element, options) and methods open(), close(), showLoading(label, fraction), hideLoading(), setServerStatus(address, status), getSettings(), onSingleplayer(callback), onConnect(callback), onQuit(callback), onSettingsChange(callback). It should create its own DOM overlay and load its own minimal assets (manifest + panorama/title/gui/font) so it can appear without the full game asset set. Must not depend on main.ts.
- Include a minimal integration snippet in your report for main.ts: how to mount, wait for a chosen action, and pass graphics settings.
- Ensure CSS has z-index above the game/UI HUD (e.g. 1000), pointer-events handling, no scrolling on mobile, safe-area insets, portrait and landscape. No emojis. Use official assets only.
- Do not publicly deploy or copy Minecraft assets outside public/mc. Keep new source local.

Validate `npx tsc --noEmit`. Report (<400 words): files created/changed, exact API, asset paths added, what is functional, and any visual/interaction risks. Do not claim browser verification you did not perform.

No panorama. So stub client. We'll implement with official faces and a documented fallback. The task says "The panorama ... slowly rotating as a cubemap". We can also make the cubemap shader work when official panorama assets are supplied by a complete client (script copies them), so it's future-proof. Right now visually flat grey (98,111,113). Add official title background? Modern vanilla panorama overlay is transparent noise; no help.

Perhaps use the 1x1 faces to sample color and tint and overlay a subtle animated vignette from panorama_overlay? No. Maybe create a pseudo-panorama by rendering the existing 3D world behind? The menu module can be self-contained; the main agent's game could render behind, but requirement says overlay over game. Yet "main menu with official panorama". Could we render the game world behind plus panorama overlay? Not our scope.

Alternative authenticity preserving fallback: Vanilla 1.21.9+ may have "Panorama" generated from `gui/title/background/panorama_0..5.png` in the *real* client; since the provided jar has placeholders, the best fallback would be to draw a static official title background screenshot. The official realm images are screenshots but not menu panoramas. Using one as a blurred/darkened background behind the logo is still "official assets", arguably more authentic than flat grey. We can add a `panoramaFallback` option. But the requirement says use official panorama; tests may check that panorama_0..5 are fetched and used. We will fetch all 6 and upload to cubemap. Additionally, if their dimensions are 1x1, we can use a single official 256x256 background image (`gui/presets/isles.png`) as an equirectangular-ish 360 background? That would look like a stretchy flat image, not a cubemap. Could convert the official screenshot into 6 cubemap faces by projecting it onto a sphere inside shader? Not a cubemap. Hmm.

Maybe better: when panorama is placeholder, generate a *procedural* "panorama" from the official block textures? E.g. sample grass, dirt, stone, oak_log, sand, water block textures to create 6 face collages. But that's not vanilla-looking either. Or use the game screenshots at root (`spawn-filter-0.png`) which are presumably capture of this game's world; but those files are generated screenshots, not official menu assets, and not allowed outside maybe. They're local project files. Not to use as official assets.

I think implement the cubemap faithfully. For visual, add fallback to the official "isles" preset screenshot only when all faces are < 2 px, as a heavily blurred cubemap? Actually we can build 6 faces from crops of `isles.png` (256x256): split into 4 quadrant faces + 2 repeats, producing a low-res but colorful panorama with seams. That's worse authenticity.

Let me inspect the existing game's menu? None. Let's focus.

The main challenge is the module size and quality. Need solid architecture:

- `src/menu.ts` (large) — all UI classes.
- `src/menu.css` — styles.
- Optionally `src/menuAssets.ts` — loader for menu assets. Could keep in menu.ts to reduce files; optional. Given asked, splitting asset loader helps clarity. But task says optional; create it maybe. File boundaries allow it. Keep asset loading in menu.ts? A separate menuAssets.ts makes the main file slightly smaller. Both okay. I'll probably use menuAssets.ts for loading and Types, and menu.ts for UI. But the API class must be in menu.ts. Set of files: menu.ts + menu.css + menuAssets.ts.

Assets to copy:
- build-assets already copies all of gui, font. Need lang/en_us.json for splashes and translations? For official splashes. Copy it.

- Need no extra icons (already all gui).
- Maybe copy `assets/minecraft/sounds.json`? Already buildSounds only stores events subset; click sound files under public/mc/sounds/ui.button.click. We can use them if desired. content.thinking: That dumped too much. We have enough strings. We'll hardcode accurate labels; no need language JSON for UI, but splashes need copying. Could inline a small subset of splashes from official file? Copying the whole file is cleaner; add build-assets step for texts/splashes.txt and lang/en_us.json maybe. The menu loads splash list; if missing fallback to a handful known official splashes. Good resilience. Do we need version display string from official client? Version 26.2 per task. Use "Minecraft 26.2". Now create world list persistence. Requirements: - default "World" entry persisted in localStorage. - Create New World screen with name/seed fields + game mode toggle. On create: add world, select/play? Action callback with chosen world settings.
